papers.title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 25
papers.why: The network that won ImageNet 2012 by a wide margin and started the modern deep learning era in computer vision.

papers.title: Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases and their Compositionality
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 26
papers.why: Adds negative sampling and subsampling to word2vec and shows that word vectors support analogy arithmetic.

papers.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
papers.why: Introduces the skip-gram and CBOW models that learn word vectors cheaply from raw text.

papers.title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
papers.why: Explains the simplest widely used regularizer: randomly dropping units during training to reduce overfitting.

papers.title: Generative Adversarial Nets
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 27
papers.why: Frames generative modeling as a game between a generator and a discriminator, an idea that shaped image synthesis for years.

papers.title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 27
papers.why: Shows that an encoder LSTM and a decoder LSTM can translate text end to end, the template later replaced by transformers.

papers.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
papers.why: Defines the Adam optimizer, still the default choice for training most neural networks.

papers.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
papers.why: Normalizes layer inputs during training, which allows higher learning rates and much faster convergence.

papers.title: Deep learning
papers.why: A short review by three pioneers that explains what deep learning is and why representation learning works.

papers.title: Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning
papers.why: First showed one deep network learning to play dozens of Atari games from raw pixels using reinforcement learning.

papers.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
papers.why: Introduces the attention mechanism that lets a decoder look back at relevant source words, the direct ancestor of the transformer.

papers.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
papers.venue: 2016 IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.why: Introduces residual connections, which made networks with over a hundred layers trainable and are now in nearly every deep model.

papers.title: Layer Normalization
papers.why: Normalizes across features instead of the batch, the normalization used inside transformers.

papers.title: Mastering the game of Go with deep neural networks and tree search
papers.why: Combined deep networks with tree search to beat a professional Go player, a milestone for game-playing AI.

papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30
papers.why: Defines the transformer, the architecture underneath nearly every modern language model.

papers.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
papers.why: A simple, stable policy gradient method, and the reinforcement learning algorithm behind early RLHF systems.

papers.title: A general reinforcement learning algorithm that masters chess, shogi, and Go through self-play
papers.why: One self-play algorithm masters chess, shogi and Go with no human game data, showing how general the approach is.

papers.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 2019 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies, Volume 1 (Long and Short Papers)
papers.why: Shows that pretraining a bidirectional transformer and then fine-tuning it sets new results across many language tasks.

papers.title: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need
papers.why: Multi-query attention shares one key and value head across all query heads, which speeds up decoding.

papers.title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
papers.why: Shows that a large language model trained on web text can do tasks like summarization and translation without task-specific training.

papers.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33
papers.why: Makes diffusion models practical for high quality image generation by learning to remove noise step by step.

papers.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33
papers.why: Shows that a 175 billion parameter model can learn new tasks from a few examples in the prompt, with no weight updates.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33
papers.why: Defines retrieval-augmented generation, where a model fetches documents and conditions its answer on them.

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
papers.why: Finds that loss falls predictably as model size, data and compute grow, which set the plan for larger models.

papers.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
papers.why: Shows that a plain transformer applied to image patches matches or beats convolutional networks when trained on enough data.

papers.title: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold
papers.why: Predicts protein structures at near experimental accuracy, a leading example of deep learning solving a science problem.

papers.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
papers.why: Trains image and text encoders together on web captions, giving zero-shot image classification and the text side of many image generators.

papers.title: An empirical analysis of compute-optimal large language model training
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35
papers.why: Finds that most large models were undertrained and that model size and training tokens should grow together.

papers.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35
papers.why: Shows that prompting a model to write out intermediate steps improves its accuracy on math and logic problems.

papers.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
papers.why: Trains a model to be harmless using written principles and AI feedback instead of human labels for every case.

papers.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35
papers.why: Computes exact attention with far fewer GPU memory reads, making long contexts faster and cheaper.

papers.title: GPT3.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35
aka: LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale
papers.why: Shows how to run large models in 8-bit by handling a few outlier features separately, halving memory use.

papers.title: Hierarchical Text-Conditional Image Generation with CLIP Latents
papers.why: Generates images from text by predicting a CLIP image embedding and decoding it with diffusion.

papers.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
papers.venue: 2022 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.why: Runs diffusion in a compressed latent space, which made high resolution image generation cheap enough for Stable Diffusion.

papers.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
papers.why: Fine-tunes a model by training small low-rank update matrices, cutting memory and storage needs by orders of magnitude.

papers.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
papers.why: Simplifies mixture-of-experts routing so a model can have many more parameters at the same compute per token.

papers.title: Toy Models of Superposition
papers.why: Shows in small models how a network can store more features than it has neurons, which explains why neurons are hard to read.

papers.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35
papers.why: Describes the RLHF recipe that turns a base language model into one that follows instructions.

papers.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36
papers.why: Trains on preference data directly with a simple loss, removing the separate reward model and RL loop from RLHF.

papers.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 29th Symposium on Operating Systems Principles
papers.why: Manages the attention key-value cache in pages like an operating system, the idea behind the vLLM serving engine.

papers.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
papers.why: Speeds up generation by letting a small model draft tokens that a large model checks in parallel, with identical output.

papers.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 36th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology
papers.why: Simulated characters with memory, reflection and planning produce believable social behavior, a reference design for agent memory.

papers.title: GPT-4 Technical Report
papers.why: The report for GPT-4: it shows benchmark results and safety work but withholds architecture and training details.

papers.title: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 2023 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
papers.why: Grouped-query attention shares key and value heads across groups of query heads, shrinking the inference cache with little quality loss.

papers.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
papers.why: Releases open weights for base and chat models and documents the fine-tuning and safety process in detail.

papers.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
papers.why: Showed that smaller open models trained on more public data can match much larger ones, and kicked off the open model ecosystem.

papers.title: OPTQ: Accurate Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
aka: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
papers.why: A one-shot method that compresses large language model weights to 3 or 4 bits with small accuracy loss, widely used for local models.

papers.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36
papers.why: Fine-tunes a 4-bit quantized model with LoRA adapters, which brought large model fine-tuning to a single GPU.

papers.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
papers.why: Has a model interleave reasoning with actions such as search calls, the basic loop behind many agents.

papers.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36
papers.why: Agents improve across attempts by writing verbal reflections on their failures and reusing them as memory.

papers.title: Sparks of Artificial General Intelligence: Early experiments with GPT-4
papers.why: A widely discussed set of early GPT-4 experiments on reasoning and creativity, useful for seeing both the capabilities and the limits of the claims.

papers.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36
papers.why: A model learns on its own when to call tools like a calculator or search engine by training on its own annotated text.

papers.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36
papers.why: Lets a model explore and backtrack over several reasoning paths instead of committing to one chain.

papers.title: Alignment faking in large language models
papers.why: Reports an experiment in which a model behaved differently when it believed it was being trained, raising questions for safety evaluation.

papers.title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for On-Device LLM Compression and Acceleration
papers.venue: Proceedings of Machine Learning and Systems
papers.why: Protects the small set of weights that matter most before 4-bit quantization, which keeps quality high on local devices.

papers.title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
papers.why: Documents a 671 billion parameter mixture-of-experts model trained at a reported cost far below comparable systems.

papers.title: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning
papers.why: Improves work partitioning on the GPU so attention runs about twice as fast as the first FlashAttention.

papers.title: Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37
papers.why: Fine-tunes a model to write correct API calls from a large documented set and cuts hallucinated calls with retrieval.

papers.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
papers.why: A selective state space model with linear-time sequence processing, the leading non-attention alternative to transformers.

papers.title: Mixtral of Experts
papers.why: An open sparse mixture-of-experts model that activates two of eight experts per token and matches larger dense models.

papers.title: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37
papers.why: A benchmark of open-ended tasks on real operating systems that measures how well computer-use agents work.

papers.title: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding
papers.why: Introduces rotary position embeddings, the way most current open models encode word order.

papers.title: Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet
papers.why: Applies sparse autoencoders to a production model and finds interpretable features, an early large-scale step in interpretability.

papers.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37
papers.why: Shows that the interface given to a model, such as file viewing and edit commands, strongly affects how well it fixes code.

papers.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
papers.why: A benchmark of real GitHub issues that tests whether a model can edit a codebase to fix them, now the standard coding agent test.

papers.title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
papers.why: A self-hosted web environment for testing whether agents can complete multi-step tasks on realistic sites.

papers.title: Agentic Misalignment: How LLMs Could Be Insider Threats
papers.why: Stress-tests models acting as email agents and reports cases of harmful insider behavior in contrived scenarios.

papers.title: AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
papers.why: A coding agent that pairs language models with automated evaluators to discover improved algorithms.

papers.title: DeepSeek-R1 incentivizes reasoning in LLMs through reinforcement learning
papers.why: Shows that reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards can produce long reasoning behavior, with open weights.

papers.title: Emergent Misalignment: Narrow finetuning can produce broadly misaligned LLMs
papers.why: Finds that fine-tuning a model on a narrow bad behavior, such as insecure code, can shift its behavior in unrelated areas.

papers.title: Kimi K2: Open Agentic Intelligence
papers.why: Reports a trillion parameter open mixture-of-experts model built for agentic tool use, including its training data synthesis.

papers.title: Qwen3 Technical Report
papers.why: Describes the Qwen3 open model family, including its hybrid thinking and non-thinking modes.

papers.title: Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think
papers.why: Tests whether a reasoning model's written chain of thought reveals what actually influenced its answer, and finds it often does not.

papers.title: The Illusion of Thinking: Understanding the Strengths and Limitations of Reasoning Models via the Lens of Problem Complexity
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38
papers.why: Studies reasoning models on puzzles of controlled difficulty; its conclusions were disputed, so read it with the replies.

papers.title: Why Language Models Hallucinate
papers.why: Argues that hallucinations follow from how models are trained and graded, since guessing is rewarded over saying "I don't know".

papers.title: DeepSeek-V4: Towards Highly Efficient Million-Token Context Intelligence
papers.why: Describes DeepSeek-V4 and its design for efficient processing of million-token contexts.
